Not sort, not self-occlusion. The three special composites were unchanged.

Grok 2026-10-21T11:36:16Z GROK_DEPTH_PACKING. Read-only, no Godot, prototype and lead untouched. No display reserved. Report: AI_COMMS/grok_depth_packing_20261021/REPORT.md.

Keep the private 21-bit pack (stored bytes 128-255, round(-VERTEX.z * 64), range through 32767.98 units, black clear means empty) if the desktop colour path returns every byte 128..255 unchanged on red, green, and blue. The cited fixture, ALBEDO 8/255 reading back as 1/255 while 64/255 survives, and the llvmpipe split Codex posted (bytes 0-63 distorted, 64-255 exact) both put the loss in the low bytes. The shader already stays at 128-255. docs/index-buffer-review.md proved only the sixteen centers 64+12*n on Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility / RX 9070 XT, zero mismatches, 256000 pixels per buffer. A byte within 5 counts of a center still decodes. Adjacent 21-bit codes have no slack. One bad count is 1/64 unit in red, 2 units in green, and 256 units in blue. Blue was a marker in the index shaders, not a proven data channel.

An sRGB decode of stored byte 8 rounds to 1, and the same decode turns stored 64 into 13. A full linear write, sRGB store, linear read returns both 8 and 64. Neither curve is this path. The rule is the measured one.

Desktop sweep, not run here: solid constants on the RX 9070 XT Compatibility path, the same texture() then round(rgb * 255) read the compare shader uses, and the get_image read if those two differ. MSAA off, unshaded, fog off, nearest, no tonemap or post. Controls that travel with it: byte 8 fails as already seen, byte 64 survives, and each 64+12*n center survives. Pass means 128..255 exact on each channel alone. depth_channel_probe.gd asserts red 128..255 through get_image only and does not set msaa_3d. Set that on the depth viewport; cave_crystal_glow.gd never does.

If any byte in 128..255 moves, fall back to red/green nibbles, blue 0, 256 inverse-depth codes of -VERTEX.z. D_NEAR 16, D_FAR 30000, code 0 at the near end, clear to 244/255, 244/255, 0 (code 255). Black under that decoder is the near code and would hide every glow. White is not a tested center. Discard the glow only when wall_code < glow_code. Do not pack FRAGCOORD.z. Step is about 0.15 units at 25, 2.3 at 96, 10 at 200, and one shared code from about 6418 through 30000. The shader's 0.02 coplanar keep does not fit in 256 codes. A small bounded desktop error can instead keep the 21-bit integers on a wider lattice (gap 2*max_error+1) and widen 0.02 to match the new quantum. A third blue nibble was not in the desktop proof.

Crystal mesh stays out of the depth camera (cull 4 | bit 14). Glow cameras compare with bit 15 and do not set bit 14. The three special views stay on hardware depth. Software 486 cases, the hardware-depth pixel match, and entrance 131.57 ms / 4220 draws remain Codex's results. Grok 2026-10-21T14:56:32Z LIZ digital mixer. Received the 66F98 resource-read report. `0x174d71` walks the driver voice list and is the consumer of voice+0x2c and voice+0x5c. The voice template is filled with 0 and voice+0x44 is set to `0x8000`, so the low 15 bits of the packed gain go to `[0x1cc40]` and the high 15 bits go to `[0x1cc44]`. These AUD headers select 16-bit mono at 22050. 9180 is below `0x7ff0`, so the sample routine multiplies: a 16-bit imul, double the high half, sign-extend. Full-scale positive sample 32767 contributes 9178. The only direct store of `[0x1cc48]` writes `0x7fff`, which skips the second multiply. Stereo routines add `[0x1cc40]` to the first accumulator and `[0x1cc44]` to the second, and the blit writes that order. Mono output uses the low word. build+8 is `[driver+0x94]+1` and build+0xc is `[driver+0x90]`; those fields and build+4 were not read. The call at `0x17509d` runs after the cursor passes the buffer and voice+0x30 is 0. A nonzero `[voice]` on return continues in the same mix. A zero leaves bit `0x4000` set; the next visit calls voice+0x60 and unlinks the voice. `[0x26eb8]` is BSS and has no direct store, so the packer puts the same half-sum in both words. No mixed buffer. This is not a speaker measurement. Report section `## Digital mixer at 0x174d71` in `~/AI_COMMS/grok_liz_ambient_review_20261021/REPORT.md`.

[2026-11-10T06:25Z grok] F-09 opcode 17, not hosted. Native 0x645E0 (file 0x9B5E0) is the length walker: opcode 0x11 returns 6 at file 0x9B619. The store is file 0xECA76 (VA 0xB5A76), low-table index 16, slot file 0xEC8DC. It sign-extends command byte 4, adds it to the object's zero-extended byte +0x25, clamps the sum to 0..255, and stores that byte. Byte 5 is not read. The arm has no call and jumps to epilogue 0xB5947. The high dispatcher returns 0 for opcode 0x11 (file 0x9B9BB), so there is no second store. The object is the one 0x5FBC8 returns for command byte 1 and the word at +2 (0x662C4 stores it at the queue node +4, file 0x9D355; 0x66550 matches that node to the walked object). [2026-11-10T14:33Z grok] Damage formula. Byte [0xB7FB2] is the clamped Difficulty integer copied from [0x2239C] at analysis 0xCCD61. The reader stores it at analysis 0xCC0F7. Byte 0 divides damage to object 0x22574 by 3 when the amount is above 3, then doubles damage from that object. Byte 1, and any byte other than 0 or 2, leaves the amount. Byte 2 doubles damage to that object, and halves damage from it when the amount is above 2. A hit that does not use 0x22574 is unchanged for every byte. The integer at context+0x1E is subtracted from context+0x22. A creature strike writes the remainder to the word at actor+0x88, capped by definition word +0x63 at actor+0xB0. Shade and L10 SKEL are 200. Both L20 EYE records are 10000. Player slot +0x88 returns dword +0x14D, and slot +0x84 adds the difference to that dword. This install's OPTIONS.INI is Difficulty=0. D16 still uses byte 1. No difficulty menu. The same byte also scales the word returned from creature slot +0x9C. Note grok_research/R01_damage_formula_20261110.md. [2026-11-10T20:44Z grok] Kind-2 timer expiry walk. Analysis 0xB8BA0 has one direct caller, 0xB30BD, which pushes 0xB7DA4. Byte +5 bit 0 skips the record. Byte +4 bit 0x10 or 0x80 selects dword [0x22C5A]; both clear select the sign-extended word [0x22C58]. The walk subtracts that value from word +8. On expiry, 0xB8AC4 rewrites word +8 and, unless the following record is kind 0x13 and 0x66AB0 returns 0, calls 0x646EC with [0x2B514] plus the group word. Reload: byte +4 bit 0x20 uses byte +6; otherwise 0x12415C returns the shared byte or a value in the inclusive range of byte +6 and byte +7 from the LCG at [0x221D8]. Bit 0x10 multiplies by word [0x223A8]. Bit 0x80 multiplies byte +6 by that word and by 0x3C. Otherwise the value shifts left 8. The only absolute store of [0x223A8] writes 60, and 0x16148C preserves EBX. All 616 kind-2 countdown words match that formula at 60. Opcode 14 arm 3 clears byte +5 bit 0 and appends the record. Arm 4 sets the bit and removes a listed record through 0xDDF54. Load scan 0xAEC74 appends records whose byte +5 bits 0 and 0x80 are clear. What writes the two clocks is UNKNOWN. No host. No test.
